purpose: Separate current normative trade-management teaching from observed examples and unresolved discretionary inputs before any July 2026 management-path result is calculated.

normative_evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
paraphrase: The first goal is a retest of the prior high with at least two units of potential reward for one unit of risk.
Reaching the target is not an instruction to liquidate the entire position; winners should remain open until a valid exit indicator.
Taking half at the target is allowed, while the entire remainder should not be sold merely because the target was touched.
The demonstrated chart is explicitly the one-minute timeframe, and the first candle closing red is taught as a valid chart exit indicator.
The teaching example also describes scaling out progressively and reacting to a materially large displayed seller.

normative_evidence.title: Growing a $2k Account to $65,662.04 in 30 Days (My Day Trading Strategy)
paraphrase: Exit indicators apply regardless of whether the open gain is small or large and must be respected.
The enumerated indicators are a materially large displayed seller, hidden-seller absorption, a burst of red tape, a dramatic false breakout, slowing buying, and a topping-tail or red candle.
A displayed order that merely flashes is not by itself equivalent to proven persistent resistance; execution and price response matter.

normative_evidence.title: 7 Candlestick Patterns I'M ACTUALLY USING Every Day
paraphrase: Large displayed sellers, bursts of selling, large topping tails, and high-volume red candles are described as adverse evidence.
Buying slowdown or a price that stops advancing calls for unwinding or closing under the breakout-or-bailout principle.
A new low after a sequence of higher candles is treated as deterioration, but the source does not provide a complete machine threshold for every chart state.

observed_behavior_examples.title: I didn't expect this!
observed_behavior_examples.paraphrase: Ross describes one campaign with multiple adds, partial profit-taking into strength, re-adds on dips, and a stop on the remainder. This supports campaign state and scaling behavior but does not define a universal numeric schedule.

observed_behavior_examples.title: When The Going Gets Tough With A Small Account…
observed_behavior_examples.paraphrase: A half-dollar/whole-dollar trade is closed when tape progress hesitates near the intended break, illustrating that the intended destination and real-time price response jointly control management.

observed_behavior_examples.title: The Hot Streak Continues! Green on 7/7 Trades Today
observed_behavior_examples.paraphrase: A position entered for a whole-dollar break is sold when a large seller prevents the break; a later independent attempt is treated as a re-entry rather than averaging down.

observed_behavior_examples.title: A shift in the market is happening...
observed_behavior_examples.paraphrase: Ross reports taking profit after an initial squeeze and identifies repeated failure to hold a whole-dollar level with topping tails as deterioration.

observed_behavior_examples.title: The Simple MACD Strategy to Spot Big Winners Early (5,712% Example)
observed_behavior_examples.paraphrase: The source distinguishes the pre-entry 2:1 opportunity test from the realized average win/loss and instructs taking profit at an exit indicator.

two-R is a first profit milestone rather than a mandatory full-position cap
optional half-position realization at the first target
breakeven stop on the remainder after that first target
completed red candle as a causal chart-only exit signal
preserve unresolved runners rather than inventing a session-close fill
requires_equal_sensitivity_cells: ten-second entry chart versus one-minute management chart
deferred_until_data_or_rule_is_frozen: second and third scale-out target prices
cushion-dependent permission to hold through a red candle
